back: The rate of flow of electric charge: I = ΔQ/Δt.
The charge passing a point in 1 s when the current is 1 A (1 C = 1 A s).
$e = 1.60 \times 10^{-19}\ \text{C}$; every free charge is a whole-number multiple of $e$ (charge is quantised).
$I = nAvq$ — $n$ carriers per m³, area $A$, drift velocity $v$, charge $q$ per carrier.
The charge is the area under the graph of current against time.
Metals: free electrons. Electrolytes: ions. Semiconductors: electrons and holes. Ionised gases: electrons and ions.

front: Typical drift velocity in a copper wire
back: A fraction of a millimetre per second for currents of a few amperes.

front: Why a lamp lights at once
back: The electric field is set up round the circuit at nearly the speed of light, so electrons already in the filament start drifting together.
Ranked by number density of carriers: metals ~10²⁹ m⁻³, pure semiconductors ~10¹⁶ m⁻³ (rising with temperature), insulators negligible.
